extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of gasoline distribution and bulk gasoline terminal facilities, regulated entities, state/local regulators, tribal governments, and other stakeholders (e.g., public commenters and analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule text and preamble specifying applicability, definitions, emission limits, monitoring, testing, reporting, regulatory analyses (benefits, EJ, RFA, PRA), and procedural determinations for NESHAP subparts R & BBBBBB and NSPS subpart XXa for gasoline distribution and bulk gasoline terminals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetized benefits/disbenefits reporting (PV & EAV at 3% and 7%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble reports present value (PV) and equivalent annual value (EAV) estimates of monetized benefits and net benefits (monetized health benefits minus monetized climate disbenefits) for each final amendment (NESHAP subpart R, NESHAP subpart BBBBBB, NSPS subpart XXa) and cumulatively, at 3% and 7% discount rates, for short-term and long-term effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each rule the RIA summarizes PV and EAV ranges (e.g., NESHAP subpart R PV short-term $11M (3%) to $6.3M (7%); long-term $87M (3%) to $52M (7%)). The RIA includes monetized climate disbenefits from additional CO2 emissions using a 3% rate where applicable (e.g., with some subparts but not others). See docket RIA for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-monetization of certain HAP health benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA did not attempt to monetize the health benefits of reductions in hazardous air pollutants (HAP) in this analysis due to methodology and data limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization of cancer-related benefits would require central estimates of cancer risks, exposure estimates to carcinogenic HAP, and values for avoided cases of cancer. Because those inputs were not available, EPA provides a qualitative discussion of health effects associated with HAP reductions in the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of discount rates and reporting short- vs long-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic results are reported using both a 3 percent and 7 percent discount rate and distinguishing short-term versus long-term effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both PV and EAV at both discount rates for comparability; report ranges for short-term and long-term effects as the RIA does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Justice analysis methodology (use of 2016 Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For regulatory EJ analysis EPA relies upon its June 2016 Technical Guidance for Assessing Environmental Justice in Regulatory Analysis, which encourages analysts to conduct the highest quality analysis feasible given data, time, and resource constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should follow recommended approaches in the 2016 guidance and explicitly recognize analytical limitations; use the guidance to frame EJ evaluation in regulatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity demographic analysis (5 km and 50 km)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA performed a proximity demographic analysis assessing demographic groups of populations living within 5 kilometers (~3.1 miles) and 50 kilometers (~31 miles) of affected facilities and compared those data to national averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results for both buffer distances, compare each demographic group's local percent to national averages, and document facility counts used in the analysis; provide more detailed results in referenced technical reports and docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic indicators for EJ comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The demographic metrics used to identify potential disproportionate impacts include percent Hispanic or Latino, percent African American, percent Other and Multiracial, percent of people living below the poverty level, percent over age 25 without a high school diploma, and percent living in linguistic isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When local percentages exceed national averages (and especially when they exceed by large multiples), note potential EJ concerns; EPA reports specific facility counts where local percentages are more than three times the national average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on distributing modeled benefits across populations
rubrics_metrics.description: When emission impacts are based on model plants, EPA may be unable to ascertain exactly how benefits will distribute across specific populations, limiting the ability to estimate EJ impacts precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge modeling limitations and, where appropriate, provide qualitative expectations (e.g., anticipated overall improvements in human health exposures), and reference technical reports for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission reduction estimates as outcome metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA reports estimated reductions in HAP and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions attributable to each final rule (e.g., NESHAP subpart R: 130 tpy HAP and 2,200 tpy VOC; NESHAP BBBBBB: 2,100 tpy HAP and 40,300 tpy VOC; NSPS XXa: 3,000 tpy VOC; cumulative reductions reported too).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use estimated emission reductions as indicators of potential air quality and public health benefits and to inform EJ conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability criteria for Subpart XX / XXa (construction/modification date windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart XX applies to facilities with construction/modification commenced after Dec 17, 1980 and on or before June 10, 2022; Subpart XXa applies to facilities with construction/modification/reconstruction commenced after June 10, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which subpart applies by facility construction/modification/reconstruction date; the regulatory text revises headings and adds Subpart XXa with explicit applicability sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of affected facilities (gasoline loading rack affected facility and collection of equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected facility can be (1) each gasoline loading rack affected facility (total of all loading racks at a bulk gasoline terminal that deliver liquid into gasoline cargo tanks, including loading racks, vapor collection and vapor processing systems) or (2) each collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal associated with loading gasoline (lines, pumps, vapor collection and vapor processing systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must identify affected facilities per paragraph (a)(1) and (a)(2) to determine applicability and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous applicability (standards apply at all times including SSM)
rubrics_metrics.description: All standards, including emission limitations, shall apply at all times, including periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction; paragraph (c) supersedes exemptions for SSM in subpart A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must demonstrate compliance at all times; cannot rely on SSM exemptions in subpart A where paragraph (c) supersedes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of standards for newly constructed facilities upon modification
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly constructed gasoline loading rack affected facility that was subject to the standards in §60.502a(b) will continue to be subject to those standards if subsequently modified or reconstructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should treat newly constructed facilities that were subject to the 'newly constructed' standard as remaining subject to that standard after modification/reconstruction as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost exclusion for frequently replaced components in §60.15 capital cost calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain frequently replaced components' costs (pump seals, loading arm gaskets and swivels, coupler gaskets, overfill sensor couplers and cables, flexible vapor hoses, grounding cables and connectors) shall not be considered when calculating 'fixed capital cost of the new components' or 'fixed capital cost that would be required to construct a comparable entirely new facility' under §60.15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude listed component costs from capital cost calculations for the purposes of determining modification/reconstruction thresholds under §60.15; see paragraph (e)(1) for the component list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'commenced' for continuous component replacement programs
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Commenced' means the owner/operator has undertaken a continuous program of component replacement or entered into a contractual obligation to undertake and complete, within a reasonable time, a continuous program of component replacement (within any 2-year period following June 10, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when determining whether frequently replaced components are excluded from fixed capital cost calculations per §60.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-hour rolling average definition and valid data exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: 3-hour rolling average means the arithmetic mean of the previous thirty-six 5-minute periods of valid operating data; valid data excludes data collected while monitoring is out of control, while conducting repairs associated with out-of-control periods, or while conducting required monitoring system QA/QC activities. The thirty-six periods should be consecutive but need not be continuous if operations/collection were intermittent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified rules for computing 3-hour rolling averages for monitored parameters; apply exclusions consistently in monitoring/recordkeeping and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms (grouped)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule defines many terms used to set applicability and compliance obligations: Bulk gasoline terminal (throughput >20,000 gal/day), Continuous monitoring system, Equipment (valves, pumps, PR devices, open-ended valves/lines, sampling connections, flanges; includes vapor processing system except exhaust ports/stacks), Flare, Gasoline (RVP >=4.0 psi), Gasoline cargo tank, In gasoline service, Loading rack, Submerged filling, Thermal oxidation system, Thermal oxidation systems emit through a conveyance suitable for performance testing, Total organic compounds (TOC), Vapor collection system, Vapor processing system, Vapor recovery system, Vapor-tight gasoline cargo tank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators and analysts must apply these definitions to determine affected equipment and compliance obligations; many definitions include technical thresholds (e.g., throughput, RVP) and testability/monitoring implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission standard for newly constructed facilities using thermal oxidation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each newly constructed gasoline loading rack affected facility that uses a thermal oxidation system, maintain emissions to the atmosphere from the vapor collection system at or below 1.0 milligram of total organic compounds per liter of gasoline loaded (mg/L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continual compliance must be demonstrated via initial and periodic performance tests (§60.503a(a)-(c)) and by maintaining the combustion zone temperature at or above the 3-hour rolling average operating limit established during the performance test when loading product. Valid operating data exclusions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion zone temperature operating limit and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a thermal oxidation system, maintain combustion zone temperature at or above the 3-hour rolling average operating limit established during the performance test when loading liquid product into gasoline cargo tanks. Valid operating data must exclude periods when there is no liquid product being loaded and, in certain cases, exclude periods when no gasoline cargo tanks are being loaded if excluded during determination of the operating limit per §60.503a(c)(8)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the operating limit during performance testing and then monitor 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature to demonstrate compliance, applying the stated exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission standard for newly constructed facilities using vapor recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: If a vapor recovery system is used at a newly constructed facility, maintain emissions to the atmosphere from the vapor collection system at or below 550 ppmv of TOC as propane determined on a 3-hour rolling average when the vapor recovery system is operating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate the vapor recovery system during all periods when it is capable of processing gasoline vapors (including product loading, carbon bed regeneration, preparing beds for reuse), minimize air or nitrogen intrusion except as needed, and do not use gaseous diluents to achieve compliance with concentration-based standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirements for vapor recovery systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate the vapor recovery system during all periods when capable of processing gasoline vapors, including during liquid product loading, carbon bed regeneration, and preparing beds for reuse. Operate to minimize air/nitrogen intrusion except as needed for adsorption media operation or to break vacuum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure continuous operation whenever capable, document periods of non-capability, and avoid diluting the effluent with gaseous diluents to meet concentration-based limits (consistent with §60.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using gaseous diluents to meet concentration-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §60.12, the use of gaseous diluents to achieve compliance with a standard based on the concentration of a pollutant in gases discharged to the atmosphere is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on dilution with air, nitrogen, or other gaseous diluents as a compliance strategy for ppmv/concentration-based emission limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission standard for modified or reconstructed facilities using thermal oxidation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each modified or reconstructed gasoline loading rack affected facility that uses a thermal oxidation system, maintain emissions to the atmosphere from the vapor collection system at or below 10 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This higher limit (compared to newly constructed facilities) must be met by the compliance date specified (when §60.8(a) requires a performance test); follow performance testing and monitoring requirements in §60.503a and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance testing requirements for demonstrating compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Continual compliance with emission limitations must be demonstrated via initial and periodic performance tests as specified in §60.503a(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced performance test procedures and schedules in §60.503a to establish emission limits and operating parameter limits (e.g., combustion zone temperature), and use those test results to set monitoring/operating limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring data validity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid monitoring data exclude periods when the monitoring system is out of control, during repairs associated with out-of-control periods, or while conducting required monitoring system QA/QC activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these exclusions when computing rolling averages or other compliance metrics; document excluded periods and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) — ICR submission and enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities in the rule have been submitted for OMB approval under the PRA; the ICR documents (with assigned EPA ICR numbers) are in the docket. Information collection requirements are not enforceable until OMB approves them and an OMB control number is displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not consider information collection requirements enforceable until OMB approval is announced in the Federal Register and the OMB control number is added to 40 CFR part 9; include brief ICR summaries (respondents, frequency, burden, estimated cost) in preamble and docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA ICR summary — NESHAP Subpart R
rubrics_metrics.description: ICR EPA ICR number 1659.12 (NESHAP subpart R): Respondents/affected entities — owners/operators of gasoline distribution facilities; obligation: mandatory (40 CFR part 63, subpart R); estimated respondents: 210; frequency: initially, semiannually, and annually; total estimated burden: 16,300 hours/year; total estimated cost: $972,013/year. Information collection not enforceable until OMB approves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these summary figures in the preamble and docket; await OMB approval before enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA ICR summary — NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB
rubrics_metrics.description: ICR EPA ICR number 2237.07 (NESHAP subpart BBBBBB): Respondents/affected entities — owners/operators of gasoline distribution facilities; obligation: mandatory (40 CFR part 63, subpart BBBBBB); estimated respondents: 9,263; frequency: initially, semiannually, and annually; total estimated burden: 83,882 hours/year; total estimated cost: $5,001,981/year. Information collection not enforceable until OMB approves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these summary figures in the preamble and docket; await OMB approval before enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA ICR summary — NSPS Subpart XXa
rubrics_metrics.description: ICR EPA ICR number 2720.01 (NSPS subpart XXa): Respondents/affected entities — owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals; obligation: mandatory (40 CFR part 60, subpart XXa); estimated respondents: 12 (assumes four new respondents per year over next 3 years); frequency: initially, semiannually, and annually; total estimated burden: 1,132 hours/year; total estimated cost: $66,930/year. Information collection not enforceable until OMB approves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these summary figures in the preamble and docket; await OMB approval before enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) certification and small entity impact reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA certifies that the action will not have significant economic impacts on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA, and reports the number/percent of small entities affected and the percent-of-sales thresholds impacted for each subpart (e.g., NESHAP R: 2 small entities affected (5% of ultimate parent companies); BBBBBB: 116 small entities affected (42%); NSPS XXa: none identified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document small entity counts and the distribution of projected costs (% of annual sales) and explain whether any small entities will incur costs >1% or >3% of sales; include RIA details in docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) threshold determination
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA determined the action does not contain an unfunded mandate of $100 million or more and does not significantly or uniquely affect small governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the UMRA conclusion and the statutory citation (2 U.S.C. 1531-1538); note that while the action creates enforceable duties on the private sector, the cost does not exceed $100 million.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866 / 14094 — significant regulatory action and OMB review
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is a 'significant regulatory action' as defined under section 3(f)(1) of Executive Order 12866, as amended by Executive Order 14094, and was submitted to OMB for EO 12866 review; documentation of changes made in response to review is in the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide RIA and documentation in the docket; acknowledge OMB review and make available changes in response to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism (EO 13132) determination — no federalism implications
rubrics_metrics.description: The action does not have federalism implications and will not have substantial direct effects on the States or the distribution of power among levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this determination in the preamble and explain why federalism implications are absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation (EO 13175) determination and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: The action does not have Tribal implications because identified affected facilities are not owned/operated by Tribes nor located on Tribal lands; EPA offered government-to-government consultation by letter to all federally recognized Tribes; no Tribes requested consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document outreach to Tribes, the absence of identified Tribal facilities, and any responses; follow EPA Policy on Consultation with Indian Tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's health (EO 13045) applicability determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is not subject to EO 13045 because EPA does not believe the environmental health or safety risks addressed present a disproportionate risk to children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale (e.g., final rules lower gasoline vapors and are projected to improve overall health including children) when stating EO 13045 inapplicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy impacts (EO 13211) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is not a 'significant energy action' because it is not likely to have a significant adverse effect on the supply, distribution, or use of energy; EPA expects minimal impacts on crude oil/fuel production and imports/exports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimates and reference RIA Chapter 5 for more detailed energy effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (NTTAA) technical standard selection
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA decided to use EPA Method 18 rather than ASTM 6420-18 because ASTM 6420-18 has a limited analyte list and is not suitable for analyzing many compounds expected in gasoline vapor; using ASTM would be impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reasons for selecting EPA Method 18 over a voluntary consensus standard and explain impracticality of the voluntary standard in the preamble/docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 12898 / EO 14096 EJ conclusions for subparts
rubrics_metrics.description: For NESHAP subparts R and BBBBBB, EPA believes existing conditions may result in disproportionate adverse effects on communities with EJ concerns and that this action is likely to reduce those effects; for NSPS subpart XXa, EPA cannot practicably assess whether the action will create new disproportionate effects because locations of future affected sources are unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reasoning linking demographic analysis and emissions reductions to EJ outcomes; note limitations for standards that apply to future, as-yet-unknown facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) — major rule determination and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is subject to the CRA; EPA will submit a rule report to each House of Congress and the Comptroller General. The action is a 'major rule' as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit the CRA report and include the major rule designation in the rulemaking administrative record.
